## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Sahetukaduka* (Patthana 14.2) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* (*patthana*) section of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It constitutes the dyad (*duka*) dealing with states "accompanied by root, and unaccompanied by root" (*sahetuka* and *ahetuka*) within the systematic exposition of conditional relations in the *Duka-Paṭṭhāna* [Nyanatiloka 2007a; Nyanatiloka 2007b].
No historical or curated parallels in other Buddhist languages are reported for this text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Machine analysis by DharmaNexus registers extensive Pali-internal text reuse reflecting the standardized combinatory matrices of the *Paṭṭhāna*, detecting 246 matching passages across 46 other Pali Abhidhamma texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual reuse partners include *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 20 matches, longest segment spanning §3.1_0–4.1 ↔ §4.1_0–5.1), *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2; 14 matches), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1; 27 matches), *Hetugocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.2; 14 matches), and *Sahetukadukādi, Hetuduka* (Patthana 12.7; 5 matches) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches are recorded with a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus].
